title: Isandro and the Veil
premise: Ada Crane fled her hedge-witch mistress with nothing but a talent for numbers and a stolen ledger, and found refuge keeping accounts for the Gilded Veil, a guild that trades in impossible things: bottled memories, borrowed luck, years of life. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark in a single night, Ada discovers the guild's founding debt is coming due — a soul sold generations ago to the court beneath the mountain, and that soul belongs to Isandro, the guild's quiet cartographer who has been her only friend. To save him she must descend into the Undercourt, where names are currency and forgetting is mercy, and bargain with a king who collects debts by unmaking the debtor. Ada wins Isandro back not by paying his price but by proving the original contract was forged — at the cost of surrendering her own true name, which she traded away to buy them both time to escape. The novel ends with the stars relighting one by one as they climb toward dawn, two people remade by what they gave up, bound now by choice rather than contract.
about_author: Orsen Nakamura is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate sales and probate ledgers before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, bargains, and the quiet violence of contracts, and live near a coastline whose lighthouses feature in everything they write.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She balances the Gilded Veil's ledgers, cataloguing impossible inventory while establishing her friendship with Isandro, the cartographer who draws maps of places that don't exist yet. Emotional beat: wary belonging — Ada has finally found a place, and doesn't trust it.

chapters.title: What the Mistress Taught
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter from Ada's POV, revealing why she ran from hedge-witch Maren Crane: Maren wanted to sell Ada's name to settle her own debts. Emotional beat: the wound beneath Ada's distrust of bargains, and why ledgers feel safer than magic.

chapters.title: A Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The border wards fall with a sound like tearing silk; every star goes out simultaneously. The guild master, Vess, goes pale over an old ledger page and orders the vaults sealed. Emotional beat: dread arriving quietly, through bookkeeping rather than battle.

chapters.title: The Founding Debt
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. She confesses to her inner circle that the guild was built on a contract: a soul sold to the Undercourt three generations ago, payment deferred until 'the night the sky forgets us.' Emotional beat: guilt calcified into duty; Vess has known this night would come.

chapters.title: Isandro's Map Has No Bottom
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She finds Isandro redrawing the same map obsessively — a descent into the mountain — though he claims not to know why. His hands shake. Emotional beat: creeping horror as Ada realizes he's being called, and he doesn't know by whom.

chapters.title: The Name on Page One
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, breaking into the sealed archive. She discovers the founding contract and reads the seller's signature: it isn't Vess's ancestor's name. It's Isandro's own, written in a hand too old for him. Emotional beat: betrayal inverted — the victim signed himself away, or someone wearing his name did.

chapters.title: He Doesn't Remember Winter
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, first time. He wakes unable to recall his mother's face, then his hometown, then whether he ever had either. Memories are leaving him like water through fingers. Emotional beat: terror of self-erasure; the debt is already collecting him early.

chapters.title: The Guild Votes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs in council scene. Vess argues for paying the debt with a substitute soul; the enforcer Bram argues for running; Ada argues for going under the mountain to void the contract itself. Emotional beat: found family fracturing under pressure, each choosing survival differently.

chapters.title: Down the Stair That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Ada and Isandro descend through a door Isandro's compulsive map-making has finally revealed. The passage reshapes itself around his fading memories. Emotional beat: intimacy sharpened by urgency — Ada narrates his life back to him as they walk, refusing to let him forget.

chapters.title: The Tollgate of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A ferryman-creature demands payment in memories; Ada pays a false one she manufactured, learning the Undercourt can be lied to if you lie precisely. Emotional beat: Ada's accounting skills become literal magic — precision as power.

chapters.title: Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Arrival in the Undercourt: a cathedral of bone-white stone lit by imprisoned starlight — the missing stars. Courtiers wear faces like unfinished sketches. Emotional beat: awful beauty; Ada understands where the sky went and what keeps it here.

chapters.title: The King Who Collects
chapters.summary: Audience with the Underking, who speaks only in questions and already knows Ada's real name. He shows her the original contract — and a second signature beneath Isandro's: Maren Crane's. Emotional beat: Ada's past and present collide; her mistress sold her friend.

chapters.title: Bargaining With a Hole Where a Heart Was
chapters.summary: Ada negotiates for time using the guild's trade-goods: bottled luck, a year of life. The Underking accepts but warns that Isandro will be fully unmade by the next moonrise regardless. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit — every delay costs something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: What Isandro Sold
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, recovered memory. As a child he traded his name to Maren Crane to save his dying mother — and Maren resold it, layered into the founding contract, making him the guild's hidden collateral all along. Emotional beat: grief and rage; he built his life inside the debt that owns him.

chapters.title: The Forgery
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Studying the contract's margins, she finds the flaw: Maren's signature postdates the contract's seal date. The founding debt is a forgery — the entire guild built on fraud, and fraud voids the claim. Emotional beat: triumphant clarity; the ledger is the weapon.

chapters.title: Evidence Before a Hungry Court
chapters.summary: Ada presents the forgery to the Underking's court, where truth-telling is enforced by the room itself. The courtiers stir; some were also sold under false pretenses. Emotional beat: high-stakes courtroom tension, Ada betting everything on exactness.

chapters.title: The Counterclaim
chapters.summary: The Underking concedes the forgery but invokes an older law: a false contract still binds whoever accepted its benefits. The guild profited for three generations; the debt transfers to all of them. Emotional beat: despair — winning the argument loses the war.

chapters.title: A Name Offered Freely
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Ada realizes a freely given name can absorb a coerced debt. She offers her true name — the one Maren tried to sell, the one she guarded her whole life — to dissolve the contract entirely. Emotional beat: the thing she protected becomes the thing she spends.

chapters.title: Unmaking and Remaking
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The contract burns; Isandro's memories flood back whole, while Ada feels her name peel away like skin. The imprisoned stars shatter their cages and streak upward. Emotional beat: sacrifice rendered intimate — she saves him by letting herself go undefined.

chapters.title: Climbing Toward Dawn
chapters.summary: Ada and Isandro ascend as stars relight overhead, each one a small victory. Ada cannot remember what she lost, only that it mattered; Isandro remembers everything, including her, and vows to carry her name for her. Emotional beat: tenderness after devastation.

chapters.title: New Ledgers, Old Hands
chapters.summary: Resolution at the guild. Vess dissolves the Gilded Veil's old contracts and re-founds it as something honest, with Ada as partner despite having no name to sign — Isandro signs hers beside his. Emotional beat: found family rebuilt on truth instead of debt.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Is Her Own Blank Page
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Ada's POV. She begins writing a new identity from scratch — not recovering the old name but choosing who to be next, with Isandro mapping the road ahead. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; identity as something authored, not owed.
